mentions.sentence: Lower limb weakness (95% in LOTS, 100% in LOSD) and later development of upper limb weakness (90% in LOTS, 83% in LOSD) was highly prevalent in both cohorts.
Lower limb weakness (95% in LOTS, 100% in LOSD) and later development of upper limb weakness (90% in LOTS, 83% in LOSD) was highly prevalent in both cohorts.
Accompanying gait disturbances, balance issues, and dysmetria (as assessed by the brief ataxia rating scale [BARS]) were also prevalent in both cohorts.
Due to shared deficiencies of ß-hexosamindase A and significant clinical overlap, the two diseases have been considered indistinguishable.
